class_method DatabricksDataSource.initializeContextState
@Override protected void initializeContextState(@NotNull DBRProgressMonitor monitor, @NotNull JDBCExecutionContext context, @Nullable JDBCExecutionContext initFrom) throws DBException { DatabricksExecutionContext executionContext = (DatabricksExecutionContext) context; if (initFrom == null) { executionContext.refreshDefaults(monitor, true); return; } DatabricksExecutionContext executionMetaContext = (DatabricksExecutionContext) initFrom; GenericCatalog defaultCatalog = executionMetaContext.getDefaultCatalog(); if (defaultCatalog != null) { executionContext.setDefaultCatalog(monitor, defaultCatalog, null); } }

@Nullable @Override public GenericCatalog getDefaultCatalog() { if (CommonUtils.isEmpty(activeCatalogName)) { return super.getDefaultCatalog(); } return getDataSource().getCatalog(activeCatalogName); }

@Override public void setDefaultCatalog( @NotNull DBRProgressMonitor monitor, @NotNull GenericCatalog catalog, @Nullable GenericSchema schema ) throws DBCException { try { super.setDefaultCatalog(monitor, catalog, schema); activeCatalogName = catalog.getName(); } catch (DBCException e) { log.debug("Error setting default catalog for Databricks", e); } }

class_method DatabricksExecutionContext.refreshDefaults
@Override public boolean refreshDefaults(DBRProgressMonitor monitor, boolean useBootstrapSettings) throws DBException { boolean isRefreshed = super.refreshDefaults(monitor, useBootstrapSettings); try (JDBCSession session = openSession(monitor, DBCExecutionPurpose.META, "Query current catalog")) { try (JDBCStatement dbStat = session.createStatement()) { try (JDBCResultSet dbResult = dbStat.executeQuery("SELECT CURRENT_CATALOG()")) { if (dbResult != null && dbResult.next()) { String currentCatalog = dbResult.getString(1); if (CommonUtils.isNotEmpty(currentCatalog)) { if (!CommonUtils.equalObjects(currentCatalog, activeCatalogName)) { activeCatalogName = currentCatalog; isRefreshed = true; } if (useBootstrapSettings) { DBPConnectionBootstrap bootstrap = getBootstrapSettings(); if (CommonUtils.isEmpty(bootstrap.getDefaultCatalogName())) { bootstrap.setDefaultCatalogName(currentCatalog); isRefreshed = true; } } } } } } catch (SQLException e) { log.debug("Failed to get current catalog using CURRENT_CATALOG() query", e); } } catch (Exception e) { log.warn("Error refreshing catalog defaults for Databricks", e); } return isRefreshed; }

Databricks connections now use a dedicated execution context that discovers and tracks the server's current catalog, can seed an empty bootstrap catalog setting, and copies a default catalog into derived contexts. Catalog-selection failures are logged and suppressed rather than propagated.

[inference, not verified] A failed catalog switch is suppressed, so a caller can continue after requesting a new catalog while the underlying connection and activeCatalogName remain on the previous catalog. If callers rely on the declared throwing contract to prevent further work, subsequent operations could target an unintended catalog.

[inference, not verified] When activeCatalogName is nonempty, default-catalog lookup returns the data-source lookup result directly. If metadata has not loaded or cannot resolve that server-reported name, callers may receive null rather than the superclass default fallback.
The supplied context does not show which lifecycle paths invoke createExecutionContext and initializeContextState, or which kinds of Databricks sessions receive the new behavior.

It is not established that every context and initFrom value reaching initializeContextState was created as DatabricksExecutionContext; inherited or alternate construction paths must be checked against the casts.
The diff does not establish how supported Databricks JDBC/server versions handle SELECT CURRENT_CATALOG(), nor whether failures or result shapes vary by driver or server version.

The ownership, persistence, and sharing semantics of the DBPConnectionBootstrap object returned by getBootstrapSettings are not shown, so it is unclear whether setting its default catalog is context-local, connection-wide, or persisted.
The actual server current-catalog value, whether it is nonempty, and whether the corresponding catalog is present in loaded metadata cannot be established from the diff.

hypotheses.claim: setDefaultCatalog must propagate a failed catalog switch to its caller; suppressing DBCException can let execution continue against the previously active catalog after the caller believes the requested catalog was selected.
hypotheses.why_suspected: The override declares DBCException but catches and only logs it, leaving activeCatalogName unchanged. Callers therefore cannot distinguish success from failure, which can route subsequent statements to an unintended catalog.
questions_to_resolve: Which callers rely on DBCException from setDefaultCatalog to abort execution?
Can super.setDefaultCatalog fail during user catalog changes or derived-context initialization while leaving the connection on its prior catalog?

hypotheses.claim: getDefaultCatalog must not return null solely because activeCatalogName is nonempty but the data-source metadata cache cannot resolve that name; it should retain the superclass default as a fallback.
hypotheses.why_suspected: The new override bypasses super.getDefaultCatalog whenever activeCatalogName is set and directly returns getDataSource().getCatalog(activeCatalogName), whose result may be null when metadata is not loaded, filtered, stale, or case-mismatched.
questions_to_resolve: Can getDataSource().getCatalog return null before catalogs are loaded or for a valid server-reported catalog?
Do consumers of getDefaultCatalog assume a non-null inherited default when one was previously available?

hypotheses.claim: A derived Databricks execution context must inherit the source context's default schema as well as its catalog; initializing it by calling setDefaultCatalog with a null schema may leave unqualified SQL executing in a different schema.
hypotheses.why_suspected: The new initializeContextState override does not delegate to inherited initialization when initFrom is present and copies only getDefaultCatalog, explicitly passing null for the schema argument.
questions_to_resolve: Does the superclass initializeContextState copy both catalog and schema from initFrom?
When setDefaultCatalog receives null schema, does it preserve, infer, or clear the source context's active schema?
Are derived contexts used for statements containing unqualified object names?

hypotheses.claim: initializeContextState must accept every legal initFrom context supplied by the inherited lifecycle; the unconditional DatabricksExecutionContext cast must not throw ClassCastException for an inherited or alternately constructed JDBCExecutionContext.
hypotheses.why_suspected: Although the new factory creates DatabricksExecutionContext instances, initializeContextState also casts the independently supplied initFrom value without checking its type, and the available evidence does not establish that all lifecycle paths obtain it from this factory.
questions_to_resolve: Which lifecycle paths call initializeContextState, and how is initFrom constructed on each path?
Can inherited initialization, metadata contexts, reconnection, or context cloning supply a plain GenericExecutionContext or JDBCExecutionContext?
